Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 45, "heading": "CHAPTER 43. ANOTHER RETROSPECT", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u045-b0030", "target": "Эта тема так чревата опасностью для шляпки, что мисс Лавиния вскрикивает ещё раз и просит меня понять, что на Дору можно только смотреть и ни в коем случае не прикасаться к ней. И вот Дора стоит минуту-две в восхитительном смущении, чтобы ею полюбовались; а потом снимает шляпку — как естественно она выглядит без неё! — и убегает с ней в руке; и вновь сбегает вниз, танцуя, в своём привычном платье, и спрашивает Джипа, есть ли у меня прекрасная маленькая жена и простит ли он её за то, что она выходит замуж, и опускается на колени, чтобы заставить его встать на кулинарную книгу в последний раз в её девичьей жизни.", "source_sha256": "7f98b4b8fd95899c5d7104f21678b9c0ac13d1a7433f891626fecfaab933fae1", "target_id": "ru-en85-u045-b0030", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "870ce2e75441b65aa7f0463c50fbe358a9f47a9f520340d65dee6e060f648ebf"}, {"source_id": "en85-u045-b0031", "target": "Я иду домой, ещё более неверящий, чем когда-либо, в квартиру, которую снимаю неподалёку; и встаю очень рано утром, чтобы поехать на Хайгейтскую дорогу и встретить тётушку.", "source_sha256": "e1c950233c7e5d34f21c8fb82f06e84f38e923f64432cb3e797ff35f421c0360", "target_id": "ru-en85-u045-b0031", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "a7a16968371fb86e0bde8a2a78c0891c67ccb5e52c0484e78ba2a6bbc2c3e2ba"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 43, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u045-b0032", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I have never seen my aunt in such state. She is dressed in lavender-coloured silk, and has a white bonnet on, and is amazing. Janet has dressed her, and is there to look at me. Peggotty is ready to go to church, intending to behold the ceremony from the gallery. Mr. Dick, who is to give my darling to me at the altar, has had his hair curled. Traddles, whom I have taken up by appointment at the turnpike, presents a dazzling combination of cream colour and light blue; and both he and Mr. Dick have a general effect about them of being all gloves.", "sha256": "4f199aa8e0ff1fb1f0c22c28560ed0a2730f979791fe82270456d9fd08c5de27", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[32]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0033", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "No doubt I see this, because I know it is so; but I am astray, and seem to see nothing. Nor do I believe anything whatever. Still, as we drive along in an open carriage, this fairy marriage is real enough to fill me with a sort of wondering pity for the unfortunate people who have no part in it, but are sweeping out the shops, and going to their daily occupations.", "sha256": "93c3bc97d7fcda2fc3f42482a07f052305669679abef8334dc5a19c25449061d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[33]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0034", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My aunt sits with my hand in hers all the way. When we stop a little way short of the church, to put down Peggotty, whom we have brought on the box, she gives it a squeeze, and me a kiss.", "sha256": "000c9316f5007d8f90193387c58a9faf415d471f37d331bc3695168987a6be1c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[34]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0035", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘God bless you, Trot! My own boy never could be dearer. I think of poor dear Baby this morning.’ ‘So do I. And of all I owe to you, dear aunt.’", "sha256": "44f6f7bf0f4f0598abe61bf2a6333e6f116253fe4e6769567d2053350b81932e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[35]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0036", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Tut, child!’ says my aunt; and gives her hand in overflowing cordiality to Traddles, who then gives his to Mr. Dick, who then gives his to me, who then gives mine to Traddles, and then we come to the church door.", "sha256": "2e48db94239f74a0a02d4d49c466e91d735f4ada23cfc77bde66469305ca7a49", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[36]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0037", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The church is calm enough, I am sure; but it might be a steam-power loom in full action, for any sedative effect it has on me. I am too far gone for that.", "sha256": "a67ee435eadc2c393bdb39a0d6de068272a54fde1a32de712c25eb5ae62a5463", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[37]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0038", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The rest is all a more or less incoherent dream.", "sha256": "fc7f3a4f1cb0106a497016b08b1fec7c2b03545547f9229b1703a826158ce47d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[38]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0039", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "A dream of their coming in with Dora; of the pew-opener arranging us, like a drill-sergeant, before the altar rails; of my wondering, even then, why pew-openers must always be the most disagreeable females procurable, and whether there is any religious dread of a disastrous infection of good-humour which renders it indispensable to set those vessels of vinegar upon the road to Heaven.", "sha256": "575b98ff1612ad01dec0e9749aaa2654a89cba3efab7ddcffea4b4d095c46746", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[39]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0040", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Of the clergyman and clerk appearing; of a few boatmen and some other people strolling in; of an ancient mariner behind me, strongly flavouring the church with rum; of the service beginning in a deep voice, and our all being very attentive.", "sha256": "91e5b2ce6aac566be23bf89c59e5bbfd0e426c117845fc3987653c44388f1b67", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[40]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0041", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Of Miss Lavinia, who acts as a semi-auxiliary bridesmaid, being the first to cry, and of her doing homage (as I take it) to the memory of Pidger, in sobs; of Miss Clarissa applying a smelling-bottle; of Agnes taking care of Dora; of my aunt endeavouring to represent herself as a model of sternness, with tears rolling down her face; of little Dora trembling very much, and making her responses in faint whispers.", "sha256": "8f07845cabf61686cfb044616634bc5ad191b3f4d0ec2450411d86465751aa62", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[41]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0042", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Of our kneeling down together, side by side; of Dora’s trembling less and less, but always clasping Agnes by the hand; of the service being got through, quietly and gravely; of our all looking at each other in an April state of smiles and tears, when it is over; of my young wife being hysterical in the vestry, and crying for her poor papa, her dear papa.", "sha256": "7ca0d0bda1f55c29f30d1da8423af392a697b9fd2112786387512b2e90e6938e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[42]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0043", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Of her soon cheering up again, and our signing the register all round. Of my going into the gallery for Peggotty to bring her to sign it; of Peggotty’s hugging me in a corner, and telling me she saw my own dear mother married; of its being over, and our going away.", "sha256": "c8b6e512384080cd3f35c6a8920ba1d108c279786c1d41d7e45ab12e742b7cf8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[43]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0044", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Of my walking so proudly and lovingly down the aisle with my sweet wife upon my arm, through a mist of half-seen people, pulpits, monuments, pews, fonts, organs, and church windows, in which there flutter faint airs of association with my childish church at home, so long ago.", "sha256": "338da827d4624e9fe4c2e533c9bd3ab4fefa46df8e639bde84374df947c52510", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[44]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0045", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Of their whispering, as we pass, what a youthful couple we are, and what a pretty little wife she is. Of our all being so merry and talkative in the carriage going back. Of Sophy telling us that when she saw Traddles (whom I had entrusted with the licence) asked for it, she almost fainted, having been convinced that he would contrive to lose it, or to have his pocket picked. Of Agnes laughing gaily; and of Dora being so fond of Agnes that she will not be separated from her, but still keeps her hand.", "sha256": "28090b0b5e29254dff15bb617847bfbff59e929dc081ee995be92cf8bb980398", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[46]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0046", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Of there being a breakfast, with abundance of things, pretty and substantial, to eat and drink, whereof I partake, as I should do in any other dream, without the least perception of their flavour; eating and drinking, as I may say, nothing but love and marriage, and no more believing in the viands than in anything else.", "sha256": "d43fe0925cc63e3b30aa7535e9d33208a4b6a1e3a1b8bc905fc48aa1e8946b0d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[47]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0047", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Of my making a speech in the same dreamy fashion, without having an idea of what I want to say, beyond such as may be comprehended in the full conviction that I haven’t said it. Of our being very sociably and simply happy (always in a dream though); and of Jip’s having wedding cake, and its not agreeing with him afterwards.", "sha256": "f2f0d34f08685c9259d80032691a519b84e65089550d7a4f86372e5adb7af071", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[48]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0048", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Of the pair of hired post-horses being ready, and of Dora’s going away to change her dress. Of my aunt and Miss Clarissa remaining with us; and our walking in the garden; and my aunt, who has made quite a speech at breakfast touching Dora’s aunts, being mightily amused with herself, but a little proud of it too.", "sha256": "c2e623cb3ec51826fd78834a94c30328a02819f54a23c50a9801d15901ea843d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[49]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0049", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Of Dora’s being ready, and of Miss Lavinia’s hovering about her, loth to lose the pretty toy that has given her so much pleasant occupation. Of Dora’s making a long series of surprised discoveries that she has forgotten all sorts of little things; and of everybody’s running everywhere to fetch them.", "sha256": "1142deb7707e693463065e0471e654fe8c2bac69ec553dc3bb0303b7d4c975a2", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[50]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0050", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Of their all closing about Dora, when at last she begins to say good-bye, looking, with their bright colours and ribbons, like a bed of flowers. Of my darling being almost smothered among the flowers, and coming out, laughing and crying both together, to my jealous arms.", "sha256": "309380d98319c724095183253fe5d7db7916e70deeae5e2128302058be4d812c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[51]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0051", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Of my wanting to carry Jip (who is to go along with us), and Dora’s saying no, that she must carry him, or else he’ll think she don’t like him any more, now she is married, and will break his heart. Of our going, arm in arm, and Dora stopping and looking back, and saying, ‘If I have ever been cross or ungrateful to anybody, don’t remember it!’ and bursting into tears.", "sha256": "be085553fa95151e691e197c37e7d6b1986fc86c0661a724929770e52b0ac112", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[52]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0052", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Of her waving her little hand, and our going away once more. Of her once more stopping, and looking back, and hurrying to Agnes, and giving Agnes, above all the others, her last kisses and farewells.", "sha256": "e0497bd1308c54dad8728614003f6bc4e3e4cbe953f44cb613b31d96c776069c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[53]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0053", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "We drive away together, and I awake from the dream. I believe it at last. It is my dear, dear, little wife beside me, whom I love so well!", "sha256": "9923d827b7f29ca020ba3d2c95356879ea458676a05e2f0ce0b79c0a0061f2df", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[54]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0054", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Are you happy now, you foolish boy?’ says Dora, ‘and sure you don’t repent?’", "sha256": "0b5ec25c799af118d604a8bfa2feeb22970a66465815eb35ba5be3ea4704f401", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[55]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u045-b0055", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I have stood aside to see the phantoms of those days go by me. They are gone, and I resume the journey of my story.", "sha256": "c9c04e4dca33dad901df91cbd421917f9ca7a3dd08e40010d53d7a44768500d1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[50]/p[56]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
